title: bora x GooeyPi - paridade seletiva
description:
Épico do projeto de planejamento `oss-team/ceo-oss/projetos/bora-match-gooeypi`
(charter + prd + `01-pensar/plano.md`, APROVADO 2026-08-26 após 3 voltas de
verificação).

CONTEXTO: o GooeyPi (am-will/gooey-pi, Electron, MIT) é um cliente GUI fino
sobre os mesmos harnesses que o bora roda em PTY. Metade das features dele
existe PORQUE ele é Electron e está fora de escopo. Este épico é a metade que
cabe num terminal.

## O que a verificação derrubou — NÃO REABRIR

- **Agendamento não é código do bora.** O `schedule:` do Dagu exige daemon
  (`dagu scheduler`), o que o invariante do muiraquitã proíbe
  (`muiraquita-cli/AGENTS.md:142`). `launchd` + `dagu start` SEM `schedule:`
  cobrem recorrência, `CRON_TZ`, `skip_if_successful` e `dagu history` — melhor
  do que um `bora schedule` faria. Sobrou convenção `.bora/schedule.yml`, que
  migra para `projetos/muiraquita-cli`. **Não criar `src/persist/schedules.rs`.**
- **`bora activity` não é verbo novo.** `bora agent list --json` já é a visão
  agregada (`collect_agent_infos`, `src/app/agents.rs:23`), já está na allowlist
  MCP (`src/mcp/tools.rs:30`) e cobre 6 dos 10 campos pedidos.
- **Paridade dos 11 verbos de CLI de `todo`/`scratchpad`/`project`: cancelada.**
  MCP escreve, `north` lê.
- **`failed` fica fora.** `pane report-result` é evento fire-and-forget, decisão
  declarada em `src/api/schema/panes.rs:383-385`.
- **Vocabulário de estado reusa `AgentStatus`** (`idle|working|blocked|done|
  unknown`) — as mesmas palavras que `bora agent wait --until` já aceita. Zero
  enum novo.
- **PTY não vira RPC JSONL.** É o que dá reattach, handoff e SSH.
- **Dois campos que eu pedi e não existem:** `agent_kind` era duplicado
  (`AgentInfo.agent` já é o kind) e `message` não tem fonte automática. Nenhum
  dos dois entra.

## Ordem

`M7 → M1 → M3 → M5 → M4 → M6`

M7 primeiro porque é a única lacuna que o próprio código do bora admite por
escrito (`src/persist/pending_prompts.rs:16-19`) e a única que dói no caminho
normal, não só na falha.

title: sidebar: attachment registry — anything attachable to a workspace
description: PROMOTED by owner design decision 2026-08-24: "A grande sacada do nosso e que a gente vai poder agrupar como quiser. Entao tudo e uma workspace. E a workspace a gente pode abrir dela algumas coisas: o PR dessa workspace, como e que ela esta, se tem uma todolist, ou comando pra ficar checando." Solo (soloterm.com, the named quality bar) has a FIXED hierarchy: project -> processes. Ours is arbitrary, and the workspace is a container of attachments. That is a model claim, not a styling one, which means the attachment mechanism is not adjacent to sidebar quality, it IS sidebar quality: a beautiful sidebar with four hardcoded attachment kinds does not support the claim. This was option C in .local/prd/plugin-extensibility.md, previously deferred until five or six sections existed so the shape of what varies would be observable rather than guessed. That precondition is now met: PullRequests is the fifth ProjectSection, landing in the current wave. Two structural obstacles are unchanged and are NOT waived by the promotion. First, the no-allocation-on-render-path rule: resolve_section_order returns a fixed-size [ProjectSection; N], never a Vec, citing AGENTS.md Multiplicative performance paths (see the comment at src/ui/sidebar/project_view.rs:568-571) because this runs per-render x per-pane x per-client. A dynamic count of providers is a Vec by construction, so this needs fixed-capacity storage or a caller-owned buffer. Second, the three-pass lockstep: workspace_list_visible_count, workspace_list_areas_for_entries and render_workspace_list all iterate one Vec<WorkspaceListEntry> and must all derive height from entry_row_height (sidebar.rs, see its doc comment); silent disagreement between passes is the failure mode the repo characterization test exists to catch. Also note deepseek-harness solves click-binding with lexical closures, which a Rust host with out-of-process plugins cannot copy, so action ids (bora-1e9) are a prerequisite rather than an alternative. Full comparison of all three prior-art repos in .local/prd/plugin-extensibility.md; bar analysis and what Solo actually renders in .local/prd/sidebar-gauntlet.md.
acceptance_criteria: A workspace-level or project-level attachment band can be contributed without editing the ProjectSection enum, and the four existing bands plus PullRequests are expressed through the same mechanism rather than living beside it. Ownership is enforced, not conventional: a contributor may only place a band where it declared it may, following the one enforcement idea worth taking from deepseek-harness. Nothing allocates on the per-render path: prove it by keeping a fixed-capacity shape and stating the cap. All three lockstep passes stay in agreement, proved by the existing characterization test extended to the new variant. A contributed band that errors renders an explicit error row, never a silently empty band. Tests plus a mutation proof per behavioural test. Decide and record whether contribution is in-binary only, config-declarable, or plugin-declarable, with the reason; bora-1e9 action ids are the click-dispatch prerequisite either way.
close_reason:
Landed. ProjectSection, the closed 5-variant enum, is gone. A sidebar band is now a SectionDescriptor in a const REGISTRY carrying its wire name, glyph, label, counter format, bullet style, the SectionLevel it may appear at, and a row-pushing fn pointer. Adding a band costs a registry entry plus one function: two sites, measured down from nine. The nine were an enum variant, a fixed-length ALL array whose size cascaded into three signatures, and seven match arms across two files of which four were silent wildcards the compiler would never have caught.

DECISION RECORDED, as the acceptance criteria required: contribution is IN-BINARY const registry only, not config-declarable and not plugin-declarable. The reason is that the remaining obstacle is not the band mechanism, it is the ROW mechanism. A new row SHAPE still cascades through entry_row_height, both apply_hidden_filter matches, actions.rs and input/sidebar.rs, all exhaustive, so a plugin-declared band today would have nothing to render but the generic SectionHeader/SectionItem rows it does not control. Shipping a plugin surface on top of that would be a promise the row layer cannot keep. The descriptor shape is deliberately exactly what a non-const provider would need, and the test that proves the two-site cost does it with a descriptor that is NEVER added to REGISTRY, which is structurally the same thing a runtime provider is. Generic rows are the next bead.

Both structural obstacles named in this bead were honoured rather than waived. No allocation on the render path: REGISTRY is &[&SectionDescriptor] with no length in its type, so SECTION_COUNT = REGISTRY.len() and every downstream fixed-size array recomputes on append; ordering returns [&SectionDescriptor; SECTION_COUNT] and level filtering is a borrowing iterator, never a Vec or Box<dyn>. The three-pass lockstep holds: both characterization tests pass unchanged. Ownership is enforced structurally rather than by convention, which was the one idea worth taking from deepseek-harness: level is DECLARED by the descriptor instead of imposed by two hand-maintained narrowing functions, which is why the unreachable!() arm that existed only because the old shape could not express 'this band is worktree-level' is deleted rather than moved. Error rows survive: a band whose provider fails still renders an explicit row, never a silently empty band.

The enabler was normalizing the push context. The seven push functions had non-uniform signatures — one took a &[String] selection, one took &Workspace instead of indices, two took a bare slug, one added a &HashSet<String> — so a naive function-pointer table does not compile. SectionPushCtx, a Copy all-borrowed enum, is what made the table possible and must not be simplified back.

10 of 10 leaf gates met plus 18 integration gates. just check: 4069 passed, 0 failed, up 17 tests. Three lead-run mutations re-verified the leaves independently rather than trusting their reports, and one of them found a real hole in a leaf's own test set, now closed. Two production bugs were found and fixed on the way, neither of them in scope: an unconditional DIM that muted the red 'blocked' label on every inactive row, and an aggregate fold whose result depended on HashMap iteration order rather than on state.

title: render: toggle_zoom and close_pane may reflow without requesting a full repaint
description:
Same class as the switch_workspace / switch_workspace_tab bug fixed 2026-08-25, found while auditing for siblings of it.

Both AppState::toggle_zoom (src/app/actions.rs:1999) and AppState::close_pane (src/app/actions.rs:2015) change which panes occupy the terminal area without changing the outer terminal's (cols, rows). Per the binding rule at AGENTS.md 'Layout changes must force a repaint, not just a re-render', that is exactly the shape that needs AppState::request_full_repaint(), because both transport encoders decide full-vs-diff purely from whether the outer dimensions changed. Neither calls it.

NOT fixed on the spot on purpose, and the reason matters: there is no observed report for either, and unlike a workspace switch they may already be covered by a different mechanism. Zoom goes through apply_pane_zoom, and close_pane removes a pane and triggers a resize of the survivors — a per-pane dimension change IS something the encoder can see, so these two may be fine for a reason that does not apply to workspace switching, where every pane keeps its size and only its contents change. Adding an unconditional repaint to both would mask that distinction rather than test it, and a repaint that fires when nothing moved is indistinguishable from having no gate at all.

The user-visible symptom to look for, by analogy with the workspace bug: the action appears to do nothing, the user repeats it, and the state log shows every attempt succeeding. That signature — correct state transitions plus a screen that does not move — is what identifies this class, and it is nearly undiagnosable from the code alone.
acceptance_criteria: For each of toggle_zoom and close_pane, determine by MEASUREMENT whether the visible terminal actually desyncs: drive the action against a real client and observe, or trace whether the survivors' resize already trips the encoder's dimension check. Then either route it through request_full_repaint() gated on an actual change, with a two-sided test in the shape of switching_workspace_requests_a_full_repaint_only_when_it_actually_changes, or record in a comment on the function why it does not need one. Do not add an unconditional repaint to either.

title: ui: four copies of the agent state label, already disagreeing on Unknown
description:
Measured 2026-08-24 while verifying that the attention-ranking unification (c07e2ff2) had not left a sibling duplication behind. It had.

Four independent copies of the (AgentState, seen) -> label-text mapping:
- src/ui/status.rs:300 state_label            -> Unknown maps to "idle"
- src/ui/navigator.rs:538 display_state       -> Unknown maps to "unknown"
- src/app/actions.rs:906 state_label_text     -> Unknown maps to "unknown"
- src/ui/sidebar.rs:270 agent_panel_status_key -> Unknown maps to "unknown"

They agree on Blocked/Working/Idle-unseen/Idle-seen and disagree on exactly one input, so the same pane running a plain shell is described as 'idle' by the sidebar's state label and 'unknown' by the navigator and by the actions label. This is the same drift class as the six attention-ranking copies unified in c07e2ff2 and the check_status rollup fixed earlier the same day, and it has already drifted rather than merely being at risk of it.

NOT fixed on the spot on purpose: the divergence may be deliberate and the resolution is a product decision, not a refactor. AgentState::Unknown is documented as 'plain shell or unrecognized program', and calling a plain shell 'idle' is arguably the friendlier user-facing word while 'unknown' is the more honest one. Silently changing a user-visible string during an unrelated wave is the wrong way to decide that.

One of the four is legitimately different in KIND and should probably stay separate even after unification: agent_panel_status_key feeds config lookup for per-status row overrides in [ui.sidebar.agents], so its strings are a config contract a user writes in their config.toml, not display text. Changing it is a breaking config change; changing the display words is not.
acceptance_criteria: Decide whether a plain shell reads as 'idle' or 'unknown' to the user, and say which and why. Then one owner for the display mapping with the other display call sites delegating to it, and a test asserting the surfaces cannot disagree — mirroring the invariant test added for attention_priority/display_priority in src/detect/mod.rs. agent_panel_status_key stays separate if kept, with a doc comment saying it is a config key and not display text, so the next person does not 'unify' it and silently break someone's config.toml.

title: plugins: per-plugin scoped RPC table instead of the whole wire protocol
description: The one thing worth stealing outright from deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and the only genuine capability gap found while answering the dynamic-sidebar question. Today src/api/server.rs:1066 is a flat match on request.method with NO per-caller capability check, so a plugin subprocess has exactly the reach of the bora CLI: workspace.*, worktree.create/open/remove, tab.*, pane.split/send_input/zoom/close, agent.start/prompt/send_keys, channel.*, project.*, todo.*, scratchpad.*, server.reload_config, server.stop. Every plugin gets all of it, forever, because HERDR_SOCKET_PATH is set unconditionally in the shared start_plugin_command (src/app/api/plugins/runtime.rs:40-44) for startup hooks, event hooks, actions and panes alike. dsh solves this with a narrow, package-private, JSON-only Client->Host RPC channel: the host half registers methods with harness.handle(method, handler) and the client half calls host.call(method, args), explicitly NOT the general remote-service mechanism, with disposal tied to the plugin lifecycle (SKILL.md:321-348). Note what this bead is NOT: it is not a prerequisite of bora-1e9. The measured reason is that a context-menu item requires an explicit human right-click, while [[startup]] already runs unattended with the same full reach at every server start (src/server/headless.rs:5221), so gating the menu path alone would be theater. The boundary today is install-time trust, recorded as a dated binding rule in AGENTS.md. This bead is about narrowing the boundary itself, which is a separable and larger change. Comparison of all three prior-art repos in .local/prd/plugin-extensibility.md.
acceptance_criteria: A plugin declares the wire verbs it needs, and calls outside that set are refused with a named error rather than silently succeeding. The refusal is enforced at the dispatch site, not by convention or documentation. A plugin declaring nothing keeps working for read-only verbs or is explicitly migrated, with the compatibility decision stated. Existing installed plugins do not silently lose capability on upgrade: either the default is permissive with a deprecation path, or the break is deliberate and documented in docs/next/CHANGELOG.md. Tests prove both directions, that a declared verb is allowed and an undeclared one is refused, each mutation-proved. The AGENTS.md install-time-trust rule is updated in the same change, since it stops being the whole story once this lands.

title: plugins: activate PluginActionContext so a plugin can offer a right-click item
description: Answers the owner question "falta um botao direito do mouse pra rodar?" for the PLUGIN case. The mouse menu is not missing: bora has seven context menus (ContextMenuKind, src/app/state.rs:1346-1400; built in one exhaustive match build_context_menu_items, state.rs:1416-1644; dispatched in apply_context_menu_action, src/app/input/modal.rs). What is missing is any way for a plugin to PLACE an item in one. Evidence that the mechanism already exists and is merely scoped: build_context_menu_items already takes custom_commands: &[String] (state.rs:1419) and turns .bora.toml shell commands into menu items, and two more items are resolved from config/registry at menu-open time (flow_available state.rs:1398, dagr_available state.rs:1370). Evidence that the placement hint already exists and does nothing: PluginActionContext (Global|Workspace|Tab|Pane|Selection, src/api/schema/plugins.rs) is manifest-declarable, parsed, echoed back over the wire, and read by ZERO UI code. Evidence that the need is already proven: the dagr integration is a hardcoded action-id constant DAGR_OPEN_ACTION_ID = "open-dagr" wired through six source files, and dagr_open_action_available() does its own narrow plugin.actions.iter().any() scan instead of using the shared registry find_plugin_action (src/app/api/plugins/mod.rs:515-575, 718-735). Prior art says nobody has this: neither aemrebarut/herdr-dagr nor cloudmanic/herdr-plus can declare a menu item (upstream herdr plugin v1 docs state outright that runtime action registration and native non-terminal plugin UI are out of scope), and even deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, whose whole architecture is a generic named-slot registry, has no context-menu slot anywhere in packages/client. Full comparison in .local/prd/plugin-extensibility.md.
acceptance_criteria: A plugin declaring [[actions]] with contexts = [...] gets its action listed in the matching context menus, with no bora source change per plugin. ContextMenuKind maps to PluginActionContext, build_context_menu_items appends matching plugin actions after the hardcoded ones, and selection routes through the existing find_plugin_action rather than a new lookup. The DAGR_OPEN_ACTION_ID special case and dagr_open_action_available() are DELETED in the same change and dagr works through the general mechanism, since that special case is the tombstone proving the need. A plugin declaring an unknown or absent context is a silent skip, never a panic and never an empty menu section. Tests plus a mutation proof per behavioural test. BLOCKING PREREQUISITE to decide before writing code, not after: src/api/server.rs:1066 is a flat match on request.method with no per-caller capability check, so a plugin subprocess has the full reach of the bora CLI. Today an action only ever runs because a human pressed a key or typed a CLI command; a menu item that fires one inherits that unscoped surface. Either gate the menu-invoked path or record the accepted risk as a dated binding rule in AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Landed. PluginActionContext is now read by the menu layer: ContextMenuKind maps to a context, build_context_menu_items appends matching plugin actions from plugin_actions_for_context (enabled + manifest-available only, Global matches every menu, empty/absent/unrecognised contexts are a silent skip, deterministic qualified-id order), and selection routes through the pre-existing shared find_plugin_action rather than a second lookup. The dagr special case is DELETED, not left beside it: DAGR_OPEN_ACTION_ID, dagr_open_action_available, the dagr_available field on GroupHeader, and the request_open_dagr flag are all gone (grep across src returns 0), replaced by a generic request_plugin_action: Option<String>. dagr now works as just another plugin whose manifest declares a matching context, and it appears on every group header instead of only the channels one. The blocking capability prerequisite was resolved NO with measurement rather than assumption: run_plugin_startup_hooks fires at src/server/headless.rs:5221 at every server start with zero human interaction, through the same start_plugin_command that sets SOCKET_PATH_ENV_VAR unconditionally (runtime.rs:40-44), so an installed enabled plugin already has unattended full-wire-API execution and an explicit human right-click is strictly MORE gated. Gating only the menu would be theater. Recorded instead as a dated binding rule in AGENTS.md naming install-time trust as the real boundary, with the narrowing itself filed separately as the per-plugin scoped RPC table bead. 7 of 7 gates in gates/bora-1e9.1.md met with evidence, 8 tests, 6 mutation proofs by the builder plus 1 re-verified independently by the lead (dropping plugin.enabled reddens exactly the two predicted tests). just check: 4052 passed, 0 failed.

title: sidebar: PULL REQUESTS section — my open PRs as rows that open a worktree
description: The owner asked for this directly: my open PRs on the remote, each row a worktree that opens a terminal like any other and shows the PR status. Most of it already exists and only the sidebar surface is missing. Evidence: fetch_my_open_prs runs gh pr list --author @me --state open --json number,title,url,headRefName,isDraft,mergeable (src/workspace/git/open_prs.rs:97-156) so it is already author-scoped via gh auth; the result is cached per repo_identity in AppState.repo_open_prs (state.rs:2207) and refreshed off the render path by start_open_prs_refresh_if_due (runtime.rs:901-928, 120s, deduped, AppEvent::RepoPrsRefreshed); it already renders as a flat list in the right panel PRs tab (right_panel.rs:17,:333) and is already exposed on the wire as github.pulls_list (api.rs:1338,:1491); and the Create-worktree modal GitHub tab already turns a chosen PR into a worktree (GithubPickEntry state.rs:1687-1697, request_open_worktree_pr modal.rs:829). Two data gaps: OpenPr (open_prs.rs:7-14) has no CI status (that is a separate per-branch gh pr view fetch on Workspace.cached_check_status), and no state field. Widening the existing --json list with statusCheckRollup is one field on a request that already runs, which is cheaper than correlating two caches. Full design: .local/prd/dynamic-sidebar-design.md. This is option (a) in that doc, deliberately the hardcoded fifth variant rather than a generic registry, because the PR section is the first section whose shape does NOT fit the existing four (repo-scoped rows, click creates a worktree that does not exist yet) and that friction is what makes a registry designable instead of guessed.
acceptance_criteria: A PULL REQUESTS band renders under the project with one row per open PR authored by the user that has no local worktree, showing number, title, draft marker and CI status. Clicking a row creates and opens the worktree for that PR branch, reusing the ProjectRowTarget::OpenWorktree shape already hit-tested for unopened worktrees. The band is project-level (a PR belongs to a repo, not a worktree) and respects sections.order:. No new fetch on the render path: rows come from AppState.repo_open_prs only. Eligibility follows the existing rules — undeclared section renders nothing, a provider error renders an explicit error row and never a silently empty band. Tests plus a mutation proof per behavioural test. Open decision to confirm with the owner first: project-level and only PRs without a worktree, versus listing every PR.
close_reason: Landed end to end. A project-level PULL REQUESTS band renders one row per open PR the user authored whose head branch has no local worktree (open or unopened-on-disk), with number, title, draft marker and CI glyph, declarable in sections.order: as pull_requests. ProjectSection gained a fifth variant with ALL widened to 5 and resolve_section_order still returning a fixed-size [ProjectSection; 5] rather than a Vec, honouring the no-allocation-on-render-path rule. WorkspaceListEntry::PrRow is height 1 via its own entry_row_height arm, with arms in all three lockstep passes plus apply_hidden_filter.
